newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Globtel to launch Slovak GSM system on Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: Globtel to launch Slovak GSM system on Jan 15.

text.p: French-Slovak joint venture Globtel GSM a.s, formerly Slovtel, said on Tuesday it would launch operation of the first Slovak GSM system on January 15.
Ladislav Rehak, Chairman of Globtel's board of directors, said the consortium was considering an international syndicated loan next year to help cover its ambitious investment plans.
"We have changed the company's name to Globtel and we will launch the system under this name on January 15," he told a news conference in the central Slovak town of Banska Bystrica.
He added that Globtel was now assesing a tender for the lead manager of the planned syndicated loan, which should be of maturity between seven to nine years.
"We started with 28 offers and now we are assesing offers from 11 banks, from which we will chose the final round of four banks by mid-January, Rehak told Reuters.
He said a final decision on the loan lead manager should be taken by the end of January.
Rehak declined to elaborate on the volume of the loan, but said that banks in the tender had offered interest rates within the range of LIBOR plus 1.0 to 1.75 percent.

Rehak said that the company's basic capital now totalled 1.9 billion crowns, but added that it will be increased to some three billion through a rights issue in March. He added Globtel did not plan to trade its shares on the Bratislava bourse.

Globtel is a consortium of four Slovak state-owned energy companies, the state-owned monopoly gas distributor SPP and the private firm Hanco sro, which teamed up with France Telecom Mobile International (FTMI) to win a government tender for one of the two Slovak GSM licences earlier this year.

Hanco holds 29 percent in the venture, while power company Slovenske Elektrarne has an 11 percent stake, SPP holds 10 percent, and the remaining utilities hold five percent each. FTMI has a 35 percent share.

Bruno Duthoit, Globtel's General Director, told Reuters that overall investment into building and maintenance of the GSM network would total some six billion crowns over the next 10 years, of which 3.8 billion should be invested by September.
Globtel has invested around one billion crowns into the project since obtaining the licence in September, he said.
Duthoit said Globtel expected to recover the initial investment for building the network within seven to nine years.
The overall GSM penetration in Slovakia is expected to be some 11 percent by the year 2006, and Globtel expects to account for some 50 percent of the market by that time.

Globtel's only competitor on the Slovak market will be Eurotel GSM a.s., a joint venture between the state-run telecom monopoly Slovenske Telekomunikacie and two U.S. telecom groups Bell Atlantic Corp and US West Media Group Inc.
